endorsements.quote: Draft documentation generated by AI systems must be subject to mandatory human review of high-risk elements, including primary survey findings, neurologic status, anticoagulation history, procedures performed, and disposition decisions.
The reviewer must be identifiable in the medical record and accountable for the accuracy of the documentation.
AI documentation systems must be trained on trauma-specific conversations, tested using curated trauma scenarios, and validated for accuracy in high-acuity resuscitations before clinical use.
Ambient AI documentation systems should be audited continuously for recurrent error patterns, bias, and unintended consequences.
Documentation errors should be investigated as patient safety events.
The rate of errors should be measured and used to drive continuous improvement.
Any AI model must be tested in the same environment in which it will be used, taking into account local languages, clinical practices, and documentation practices.

unlisted_practices: Configure AI documentation systems to preserve uncertainty by allowing entries such as unknown, unable to assess, history unreliable, or pending verification rather than converting incomplete information into definitive statements.

Use structured documentation fields for safety-critical elements such as neurologic assessments, procedures, vital sign trends, and transfusion events instead of relying on unstructured AI-generated free text.

Involve multidisciplinary stakeholders, including trauma nurses, prehospital leaders, trauma program directors, and quality improvement teams, in the design, deployment, and monitoring of AI documentation systems.
Obtain explicit consent before ambient AI recording of family discussions, law enforcement statements, or social worker discussions in trauma care.

screen.reason: This is an editorial providing recommendations and proposing safety guardrails for the deployment of ambient AI documentation systems in trauma resuscitation.
